content:
Many people have complained in recent years that Apple's designs have lost some of their iconic whimsy. Well, here's the latest sign that the tide may be turning.

Hidden inside the Settings app in iOS 27, Apple has tucked away an Easter egg paying tribute to a classic Mac OS character—Clarus the Dogcow. Here's how to trigger it…

iOS 27 adds a new feature that lets users customise the intensity of the Liquid Glass transparency effect, with a slider ranging from "Clear" to fully "Tinted." You can find it on your iPhone by going to Settings > Appearance > Liquid Glass.

Within that page, Apple has included a mock website interface that lets you preview how Liquid Glass will look as you adjust the slider. There is a small scrollable area containing some text and photos of Apple Park.

Here's the Easter egg: scroll all the way to the bottom of the screen and keep pulling up with your finger, and a photo of a Clarus the Dogcow figurine will appear, right next to the pond at Apple Park. In the demo's search bar, the word "Moof!" will also show up in rainbow colours—the very sound the dogcow makes.

If you type "Moof!" into Siri via Spotlight, Siri will even reply, "Nice dogcow."

For those unfamiliar with the history, Clarus the Dogcow dates back to an icon drawn by Susan Kare for the original Mac. It was a character in the Cairo font—the classic Mac's icon typeface, similar to Windows' Dingbats. It had basically no practical use, purely a bit of fun.
